description: The chart illustrates estimated “effect” values for several morphosyntactic categories across multiple multilingual BERT variants, shown as colored bars with vertical error bars. The category axis is arranged along the horizontal direction with labels including “gender,” “tag,” “number,” and “tense” (with additional categories partially visible at the left edge), and the value axis is labeled “effect” on a linear scale with tick marks at approximately 5-unit intervals (e.g., 5, 10, 15, 20) spanning roughly from 0 up to the low-to-mid 20s. For each category, multiple adjacent bars are grouped together, each bar corresponding to a different model variant indicated by color (including several blues, greens, and reds/pinks; the legend in the upper right includes at least “XLM-R” and “XLM-R-L2”), and each bar has a black error bar extending above and below the bar height. Approximate bar heights vary by category: in the leftmost visible group, blue bars are around the mid–single digits to high–single digits, green bars are around the high–single digits to about 10, and red/pink bars reach into the high teens; for “gender,” bars range from roughly 10–12 (blue/green) up to about 16–18 (red/pink); for “tag,” bars cluster around the high teens (approximately 17–19); for “number,” bars span roughly the high teens to low 20s (about 18–22); and for “tense,” bars are in the low-to-mid 20s (approximately 22–24). The bars within each category are not stacked (they are side-by-side), there is no visible sorting by bar height within categories, and no individual bars appear specially emphasized beyond the consistent use of color and error bars.
